title: Schedule Guarantee Periods and Liquidated Damages Rates by Project Class
content:
# Schedule Guarantee Periods and Liquidated Damages Rates

Three of the six classes of Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects carry a schedule guarantee. The guaranteed period, the daily amount of liquidated damages and the ceiling on those damages are fixed per class:

| Project class | Guaranteed period (calendar days from mobilisation; 0 means no guarantee) | Liquidated damages (USD per calendar day of delay) | Ceiling on liquidated damages (per cent of contract value) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Equipment Replacement Order | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Planned Replacement Program | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Controls Retrofit Project | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Energy Retrofit Project | 120 | 450 | 5 |
| Turnkey Mechanical Upgrade Project | 180 | 1200 | 5 |
| Design-Build Infrastructure Program | 270 | 3500 | 8 |

## What the three columns mean

The guaranteed period is the number of calendar days from mobilisation within which substantial completion is guaranteed; a period of 0 means the class carries no schedule guarantee. The daily amount is what is credited per calendar day of delay beyond the guaranteed period. The ceiling is the most the damages can reach, expressed as a portion of the contract value.

## Two hypothetical readings

- On a Turnkey Mechanical Upgrade Project with a contract value of USD 300000, the ceiling is 5 per cent, USD 15000; at USD 1200 per day the ceiling is reached on the thirteenth day of delay, since 12 days come to USD 14400 and 13 days to USD 15600, which is above the ceiling.
- A Controls Retrofit Project shows 0 in every column: it carries no schedule guarantee and no daily amount, whatever its contract value.
